prompt: Close-up of curly kale, potato gnocchi, leek and smoked bacon casserole in a plain white baking dish. Soft, plump, pillow-shaped, pale cream-yellow dumplings with shallow ridges sit in thick pale ivory cream sauce, no pooled broth. Very dark olive green to almost black-green, soft, wilted kale shows tightly ruffled leaves in irregular curled pieces. Soft, glossy, flat ivory-white to pale muted green leek strips and pinkish light-brown bacon cubes with creamy off-white rendered fat and lightly browned edges are visible. A thin, patchy pale golden-yellow melted cheese layer with deeper golden-brown toasted spots and coarse, airy, irregular angular golden panko flakes covers the top. Light steam, natural sheen, clean rim. Fills 80% of square frame; 45° view, 85 mm, f/5.6, warm soft natural side light, true-to-life colours, sharp textures, blurred narrow table strip. No text, logos, hands, people or props.

visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Blanched, chopped and baked: very dark olive green to almost black-green, soft and wilted, with a light glossy sauce coating; thick, tightly ruffled leaves in irregular small curled pieces about 1–2 cm, roughly 8–12 pieces visible per portion. Clearly curly kale, with much thicker, more crinkled leaves than spinach and far darker than pale cabbage.

Briefly sweated, then baked: soft, glossy, flat strips, ivory-white to pale muted green, with slightly translucent sections and little browning; about 0.2–0.3 cm wide and 2–4 cm long, with 4–6 strips visible per portion. Flat layered leek strips rather than curved onion slices, no longer raw or crisp.

Briefly sweated, then baked: pinkish light-brown bacon cubes with creamy off-white rendered fat and lightly browned edges; about 0.5–0.8 cm each, glossy and tender with some slightly firmer edges rather than uniformly crisp, about 6–10 visible per portion. The marbled lean meat and partly translucent fat distinguish it from uniformly pink diced ham.

Baked directly in the sauce: soft, plump, pillow-shaped, pale cream-yellow dumplings with shallow ridges, about 2 cm long and 1 cm wide, lightly coated with cream sauce; exposed edges may be faintly golden, with about 5–7 visible per portion. Distinctly small ridged potato dumplings, not pasta shells or chunks of boiled potato.

Baked on top: coarse, airy, irregular angular golden panko flakes, about 0.2–0.4 cm, dry and crisp-looking, unevenly golden to deep golden brown; a thin patchy scattering across each portion rather than a countable set of pieces. Much larger and flakier than fine, sandy breadcrumbs.

Melted and baked into a thin, patchy pale golden-yellow melted cheese layer with deeper golden-brown toasted spots; faintly glossy from fat and lightly crisp at the edges. The short grated strands are mostly fused into the topping, with no countable individual pieces and no thick, uniformly stretchy cheese blanket.
